question: In which year did Subhash Chandra Bose escape from under British surveillance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1941.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 1941 **Subhash Chandra Bose escape from under British surveillance.
 
• Bose escaped from under British surveillance from his Elgin Road house in Calcutta on the night of 17 January 1941, accompanied by his nephew Sisir Kumar Bose.
 
• Later reaching** Gomoh Railway Station** (now Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Gomoh Station) in the then **state of Bihar (now Jharkhand), India.**
 
• He reached **Russia via Afghanistan.**
 
• This incident is also known as** "The Great Escape".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• He was twice elected **President of the Indian National Congress.**
 
• Bose had set up an Indian Legion in Berlin in 1941 but developed difficulties with the Germans when they tried to use it against Russia and decided to go to South East Asia.
 
• He reached Japanese-controlled Singapore from Germany in July 1943.
 
• He issued his famous call, ‘Delhi Chalo’, and announced the formation of the Azad Hind Government and the Indian National Army on 21st October 1943.
